models.purpose: Score sustainability as footprint minus carrying capacity.
models.summary: The baseline the paper rejects. A country is sustainable only when the footprint stays below carrying capacity, and the model ignores economy and society.

governing_equations.purpose: sign of the deficit decides sustainability

objectives: Score sustainability as footprint minus carrying capacity.
constraints: sustainable only when footprint stays below carrying capacity
assumptions: the measured country is stable over the window

identifiability_feasibility.analysis: weights mix entropy and expert judgment, so they are not identified from data alone

strengths: the result is a geometric relation anyone can read
limitations: the threshold factors are chosen, not estimated
missing_details: four indices were dropped for lack of data

models.purpose: Score sustainability as the product of an angle and a projection length.
models.summary: Two indices, society-economy and environment-resources, place a country in the unit square. The diagonal is the ideal direction. Harmonious development is the angle between actual and ideal direction. Valid development is the projection of the actual move onto the diagonal. Their product is the sustainable distance, compared with 0.7854.

variables.definition: society-economy index, scaled to the unit interval
environment-resources index, scaled to the unit interval
angle between actual and ideal development direction
length of the projection onto the ideal direction
product of the angle and the remaining distance

governing_equations.purpose: product of angle and distance, with a stated threshold

objectives: Score sustainability as the product of an angle and a projection length.
constraints: indices are scaled to the unit interval
sustainable only when Dt stays at or below 0.7854

parameter_estimation.method: entropy weight combined with CRITIC expert weight, checked by Kendall consistency and Spearman post hoc

assumptions: the measured country is stable over the window

models.purpose: Project Nepal twenty years forward, with and without intervention.
models.summary: Without intervention each index is forecast by ARIMA(0,1,0) with drift, chosen because the series are nonstationary and seasonal. With intervention a system-dynamics model of three subsystems links the indices and estimates its parameters by three-stage least squares. The modernization program gives the smallest sustainable distance.

education expenditure raised 1.4 percent a year
access to electricity raised 11.7 percent a year

governing_equations.source_expression: di = (Dt(x + delta_i x) - Dt(x)) / delta_i x
